summary: Intermittent finisher-starvation causing request timeouts on ultra-long max_tokens streaming requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming requests with extremely large max_tokens (50k-100k) intermittently finish sending early or return HTTP 504/Client deadline exceeded after long periods of partial output. Time-to-first-byte is normal; latencies spike toward the tail of the generation and final chunks are delayed beyond client deadlines.

Impact:
- Affected customer: LexiSearch (enterprise) using hosted API for document synthesis workflows.
- Observed on ~15% of large-output requests during peak traffic windows; otherwise successful.
- Customer observed multiple aborted exports and retries; material impact to their SLA.

Environment:
- Hosted production (prod-us-east-1)
- Streaming=true, max_tokens=80000 (customer-provided), model pinned to redwood/open-llama-13b-quant-v2
- Request pattern: long system prompt (priming ~200k chars) + multi-document context; sustained token emission for >2 minutes.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create request with streaming=true, max_tokens=80000, context ~120k tokens (multi-doc priming).
2) Send simultaneous 6 requests from a single customer API key (to exercise per-key concurrency).
3) Observe generation progress and streaming frames; measure ttfb, inter-chunk gaps, finalization time.

Observed behavior:
- First ~95% of tokens stream normally with expected throughput.
- Finalization stalls: gap of 30s-90s between last streamed chunk and final chunk, often causing client deadline exceeded or HTTP 504.
- Runtime logs show finisher queue backlog and executor slot starvation; KV-cache evictions spike concurrently.
- Some requests are dropped with 5xx from scheduler when finisher cannot obtain GPU slot for finalization.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous chunked streaming to completion without long tail gaps; graceful fallback to a smaller model variant or throttled continuation if resources constrained.

Logs & tracing:
- Traces: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-431210 (redacted)
- Grafana dashboard (tail-latency): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/finisher/stream-tail-latency?var-region=us-east
- Excerpt from runtime logs (attached as plain text):
  - "finisher.queue.wait_ms=31234; active_executors=0; idle_executors=2; kv_evictions=43"
  - "scheduler: request_promoted_to_backlog due to executor shortage"

Workaround applied:
- Support applied temporary policy: per-key concurrent request limit reduced to 3 and max_tokens soft cap at 40k for LexiSearch; this restored successful completions but reduces throughput.

Business impact / customer notes:
- Customer experiencing missed nightly exports and has requested timeboxed remediation.
- Account team escalated; customer asked for ETA for a permanent fix.
comments: Aisha Khan (2026-03-12): Ticket created after CS call with LexiSearch. They provided sample request and logs. Marking as high priority due to enterprise SLA impact.
Marco Silva (2026-03-12): Reproduced locally against prod-like cluster by replaying the supplied request; observed finisher backlog and kv-cache churn. Assigning to runtime on-call.
RuntimEng Oncall (2026-03-13): Hypothesis: long-lived KV cache for very deep context causing memory compaction and executor preemption during finalization. Captured heap and eviction traces.
Marco Silva (2026-03-13): Applied temporary per-key concurrency throttle and max_tokens soft-cap (customer config) as mitigation. Customer accepted workaround.

Support Manager - Elena Ortiz (2026-03-14): Requesting prioritized patch to finisher queue backpressure and a model-fallback policy for resource-constrained tail emissions. Please attach linked PRs and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Executor slot starvation — finalization requires an exclusive executor and long contexts hold KV resources longer, blocking other finishers.
Hypothesis 2: KV-cache eviction thrashing — frequent eviction during high-context workloads causes page faults and stalls in the finisher pipeline.
Metric snapshots (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC): finisher_queue_length peaked at 37; finisher_tail_latency_p90 = 78s; kv_eviction_rate increased 6x versus baseline.
Reproduced with controlled load: same pattern observed when simulating 4 concurrent ultra-long requests on a medium-sized pod.
Temporary mitigation (throttling) reduced finisher_queue_length to <5 and tail latency p90 to 12s for the customer traffic slice.
Next artifacts to gather: core dumps from executor if preempted, per-request KV cache sizes, and scheduling/placement logs for the affected pod IDs.
resolution: Mitigation in place: per-customer throttling and soft max_tokens cap applied (manual override). No code fix deployed yet. Next steps: implement automatic finisher backpressure that will either (a) spill long tail to a lower-cost executor pool, (b) trigger model-fallback to a smaller variant when finalizer wait exceeds threshold, and (c) improve KV eviction policy to avoid thrashing. Target patch PR scheduled for 2026-03-19; runtime team to validate with synthetic workloads and customer test.
